cosy-lesson.title: Home is a Time: Not a Place

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Belonging – a sense of being part of a particular group or place.

p.em: Example: Finding a community where you feel a sense of belonging is essential for mental health.

cosy-blockquote.p: La nostalgia ≠ La modernidad – sentimiento de pena por la lejanía o el tiempo pasado ≠ cualidad de lo moderno o actual.

p.em: Example: Sintió una profunda nostalgia por el pueblo antiguo, un contraste total con la fría modernidad.

cosy-blockquote.p: Evanescent – soon passing out of sight, memory, or existence; quickly fading or disappearing.

p.em: Example: The joy of childhood often feels evanescent once we reach adulthood.

cosy-blockquote.p: Geography – the physical features of an area; the study of places.

p.em: Example: The geography of the region changed significantly after the new dam was built.

cosy-blockquote.p: Temporality – the state of existing within or having some relation to time.

p.em: Example: Philosophers often discuss the temporality of human existence and the fleeting nature of life.

cosy-blockquote.p: Rooted – firmly established or deeply connected.

p.em: Example: Her love for the sea was deeply rooted in her childhood holidays on the coast.

cosy-blockquote.p: Transient – lasting only for a short time; impermanent.

p.em: Example: The feeling of excitement after a promotion is often transient, quickly replaced by new stress.

cosy-blockquote.p: Sentimentality – excessive tenderness, sadness, or nostalgia.

p.em: Example: His sentimentality made it hard for him to throw away even the smallest childhood mementos.

cosy-blockquote.p: Displacement – the moving of something from its place or position.

p.em: Example: The war caused the displacement of millions of people from their ancestral homes.

cosy-blockquote.p: Atmosphere – the pervading tone or mood of a place, situation, or work of art.

p.em: Example: The cozy atmosphere of the small cafe made it feel like a second home.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
Where do you currently feel the strongest sense of belonging in your daily life?
★ When was the last time you had to confront belonging in your own personal journey?

How does nostalgia for your school days differ from the reality of what those days were actually like?
★ How comfortable are you with allowing la nostalgia to guide your daily decisions?

Why is the feeling of pure, uncomplicated safety so evanescent as we grow older?
★ Have you ever felt a deep sense of conflict regarding evanescent in a relationship?

Does the geography of your hometown still hold a special place in your heart, or has it changed too much?
★ Can you share a moment from your childhood where geography felt completely natural?

How does the temporality of human life influence our desire to create permanent homes?
★ How do you personally nurture temporality when you feel emotionally exhausted?

In what specific memories are your most important life lessons deeply rooted?
★ Have you ever had to choose between social conformity and personal rooted?

Why is it that some of our most transient living situations feel the most like "home"?
★ Who in your life best embodies the essence of transient, and what have they taught you?

Is sentimentality toward physical objects a healthy way to preserve memories of the past?
★ In what area of your life do you feel sentimentality is most desperately needed right now?

How does the displacement of people across the globe change our traditional definitions of "home"?
★ How has your personal understanding of displacement shifted over the last five years?

How can you recreate the atmosphere of your favorite "home time" in your current house?
★ If you had to describe your personal experience with atmosphere in one word, what would it be?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: deeper debate and statement evaluation in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, debate and state whether you agree or disagree with these statements:

ol.li:
In the future, technology will enable us to digitize and share our experience of belonging directly. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ How would you personally adapt if belonging became entirely obsolete in tomorrow's world?

The rapid speed of modern society will eventually make la nostalgia an obsolete concept. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Would you be willing to use technology to artificially boost your capacity for la nostalgia?

Future educational systems will prioritize the cultivation of evanescent over traditional academic skills. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ How do you want future generations of your family to remember your relationship with evanescent?

As artificial intelligence advances, machines will exhibit a superior capacity for geography compared to humans. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ If you could design a futuristic school, how would you teach the value of geography to children?

In the coming decades, temporality will become a highly commercialized luxury commodity. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Do you fear a future where temporality is fully managed or monitored by digital algorithms?

The survival of human civilization will depend on our collective ability to practice rooted. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ How do you personally prepare for a future where rooted is increasingly rare?

Future generations will look back at our current understanding of transient with deep skepticism. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ If you could send a single message about transient to people living 100 years in the future, what would it be?

Global digital connectivity will make true sentimentality incredibly difficult to maintain in the future. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Would you choose to live in a futuristic utopia that completely guarantees sentimentality at the cost of your freedom?

In the future, social status will be determined by a person's capacity for displacement rather than wealth. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ What role do you hope displacement will play in your own personal future over the next decade?

A world fully governed by logic will have no space left for the mystery of atmosphere. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ If a machine could perfectly replicate your experience of atmosphere, would you still value it?

ul.li: Incorrect: I am live here since five years → Correct: I have lived here for five years / I've been living here for five years ((Present Perfect + Duration))
Incorrect: It makes me feeling nostalgic → Correct: It makes me feel nostalgic ((Make + object + bare infinitive))
Incorrect: There is a cozy atmosphere → Correct: There is a cozy atmosphere ((Spelling: atmosphere))
Incorrect: I am agree with you → Correct: I agree with you ((Verb agreement))
Incorrect: It is depend on you → Correct: It depends on you ((Verb vs Adjective))
